blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Orchestrating a supply chain ecosystem means recognising that the chain does not belong to any single company. Suppliers have suppliers. Customers have customers. Logistics providers serve competitors at the same time. Each actor has their own priorities, their own pressures, and their own sense of what the chain should optimise for.

The senior leader's job is to make the ecosystem work, not to pretend to own it. Rarely does that come from tight control. It comes from clarity of shared interest, from investments that benefit multiple parties, from information shared with discipline, and from a willingness to be the partner others want to keep.

Not only does this approach reduce friction in normal times, but it also changes everything in a crisis. The ecosystems that respond well to shocks are almost always the ones with strong underlying relationships, built deliberately, over years, by leaders who understood that ownership was an illusion and partnership was the real lever.

items.q: According to the text, who does the supply chain belong to?
options: The senior leader who orchestrates it
The logistics provider
No single company
The largest supplier
items.why: "the chain does not belong to any single company."

items.q: Where does effective orchestration come from, according to the text?
options: Owning the logistics providers outright
Reducing the number of partners in the chain
Clarity of shared interest and disciplined information sharing
Tight, centralised control over every actor
items.why: "It comes from clarity of shared interest… from information shared with discipline."

items.q: The phrase "a willingness to be the partner others want to keep" suggests that…
options: contracts should lock partners in for as long as possible
partners should be replaced frequently to stay competitive
an orchestrator earns influence by being valuable, not by controlling
loyalty matters more than performance
items.why: Inferência: sem posse ou controle, a influência vem de ser um parceiro que os outros querem manter.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Strong relationships help an ecosystem absorb shocks.
Ownership of the whole chain is largely an illusion.
A company can command a supply chain the way it commands its own staff.
Investments that benefit multiple parties strengthen the ecosystem.
items.why: Inferência: o texto sustenta que a posse é ilusão e que controle rígido não funciona.

items.q: Why does the text say resilient ecosystems are "built deliberately, over years"?
options: Because technology takes years to install
Because suppliers are slow to sign agreements
Because regulation requires long contracts
Because trust and underlying relationships cannot be improvised in a crisis
items.why: Inferência: relações fortes que respondem a choques não se criam na hora — precisam ser cultivadas ao longo do tempo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver apresentar o programa de planejamento conjunto aos parceiros. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for coming. I want to be candid about why the five of us are in this room. Between the three suppliers here and our two logistics partners, we effectively run one chain together — even though, on paper, we're five separate companies with five separate P&Ls.

For years we've each optimised our own link and hoped the whole would take care of itself. It hasn't. When demand spiked in March, none of us had the visibility to react as one, so we all held excess stock and still missed the window. That cost every party in this room.

So I'm not here to tell anyone how to run their business. What I'm proposing is a joint-planning rhythm: shared forecasts, a common view of inventory, and one agreed set of trigger points. Rarely does this kind of thing work when it's imposed, so I want us to design it together.

Let me be clear about the deal. This only holds if the gains are shared. If our forecasts help one of you cut safety stock, that saving stays with you. Not only do I want fewer surprises, but I also want each of you to walk out better off. That's the whole point.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Oliver describe the relationship between the five companies?
options: They are subsidiaries of a single parent company
They are two logistics firms supervising three suppliers
They effectively run one chain together despite being separate companies
They are competitors bidding for the same contract
items.why: "we effectively run one chain together — even though, on paper, we're five separate companies."

items.q: What went wrong when demand spiked in March?
options: One supplier withdrew from the chain
A logistics partner raised its rates without warning
They lacked shared visibility, held excess stock, and still missed the window
Prices collapsed across the market
items.why: "none of us had the visibility to react as one, so we all held excess stock and still missed the window."

items.q: Why does Oliver want the group to design the plan together rather than impose it?
options: Because the contract legally requires unanimous approval
Because his company lacks the data to design it alone
Because he wants to avoid taking responsibility
Because imposed arrangements rarely work in an ecosystem of independent partners
items.why: Inferência: "Rarely does this kind of thing work when it's imposed" — parceiros independentes precisam co-desenhar.

items.q: What does Oliver mean by "This only holds if the gains are shared"?
options: The savings must all be returned to his company
The arrangement will collapse unless every party benefits
Everyone must contribute the same amount of capital
The plan is only temporary and will be reviewed monthly
items.why: Inferência: sem benefício mútuo, os parceiros não sustentam o acordo — é a condição do programa.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's stance toward the partners?
options: Collaborative — he seeks a shared rhythm without dictating how each runs its business
Authoritative and prescriptive about their operations
Detached and purely transactional
Uncertain about whether the programme is worthwhile
items.why: Inferência: ele repete que não vai dizer como cada um roda o negócio e quer construir junto.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "To orchestrate an ecosystem is to set the rhythm without owning every instrument." To orchestrate here means to…
options: purchase a controlling stake in each partner
compose background music for events
write detailed rules for every transaction
coordinate independent parties toward a shared outcome
items.why: Orchestrate = orquestrar: alinhar atores independentes para um resultado comum, sem controlá-los.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every additional handoff between systems adds ___ that slows the whole chain down."
options: visibility
priority
discipline
friction
items.why: Friction = atrito: o entrave que cada transferência mal-integrada acrescenta.

items.q: "The underlying relationships held when the shock hit." Underlying means…
options: recently signed
temporary and informal
underneath the surface, forming the foundation
publicly announced
items.why: Underlying = subjacente: aquilo que está na base, sustentando o resto.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Ownership of the whole chain was an ___; in practice no one controlled every link."
options: priority
actor
illusion
ecosystem
items.why: Illusion = ilusão: a posse total era uma falsa impressão, tese central da lição.

items.q: In this context, each actor in the ecosystem refers to…
options: a member of the board of directors
a performer hired for a corporate event
any participating party with its own priorities and pressures
the company that owns the chain
items.why: Actor = ator: cada parte participante — fornecedor, cliente, operador — com prioridades próprias.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de parceria e cadeia de suprimentos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "All five partners will have to sign off on the joint-planning charter." To sign off on means to…
options: postpone indefinitely
quietly ignore
formally approve
comment on informally
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We'll roll out the shared-forecast system to one lane before the whole network." To roll out means to…
options: implement it in stages
cancel it in phases
keep it confidential
audit it externally
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, lançar por etapas.

items.q: "One logistics partner pushed back on sharing raw inventory data." They…
options: resisted or objected to it
approved it immediately
forgot to review it
delegated it upward
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Everyone endorsed the plan, but two suppliers never followed through." They…
options: renegotiated the terms
documented it badly
failed to carry it to completion
passed it to a subcontractor
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Trimming a day of transit time won't move the needle unless we fix the forecasting gap." This means it will…
options: provoke resistance from partners
make no noticeable difference
cost more than budgeted
take months to measure
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, sozinho não muda o resultado.
